components: enterprise assistant (approved enterprise AI tool with enterprise data protection)
prompt library (press release drafting templates based on report/briefing note inputs)
training (guidance for Communications staff on reviewing drafts, verifying quotes/sources, and using the assistant appropriately)
output.rationale: This is a classic drafting/summarisation task over internal-level information (published reports and internal briefing notes) producing a first-draft text, with a human (communications officer) always reviewing and approving before publication. There is no requirement to answer questions from a fixed, citation-backed document collection (ruling out knowledge_assistant_rag), no multi-step repeated document pipeline with routing/classification/audit needs beyond simple draft-then-review (ruling out document_workflow_automation), and no need for multiple tools used in a dynamic, unpredictable sequence (ruling out tool_using_agent). 'No AI needed' is insufficient because the core value is generative drafting of press release text from source material, which a form, search box, or static report cannot provide. The assistant_on_managed_platform pattern matches exactly: staff need help drafting from internal-level information, with human review as the safety control, low cost ($3-6/month), and risk controls (enterprise-only tool, no fabrication, officer sign-off before publication, AI Office intake, business+InfoSec approval) layered on top as governance rather than needing a heavier architectural pattern. Keeping to the simplest pattern that satisfies the 'draft' autonomy level and 'limited' risk level avoids unnecessary complexity (e.g., building a RAG index or workflow engine) while still meeting the stated requirements and risk controls.
